simple.meaning: יָחֵף (yâchêph) is a Hebrew word meaning “unsandalled.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָחֵף (H3182) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Samuel 15:30, with occurrences in 2 Samuel, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָחֵף (H3182) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָחֵף (H3182) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָחֵף (yâchêph) / H3182 is traced through 2 Samuel 15:30, Isaiah 20:2, Isaiah 20:3, Isaiah 20:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3182. yacheph יָחֵף adjective barefoot , always absolute יָחֵף Isa 20:2 4 t.; — וְיָחֵף עָרוֺם הלך 20:2 ( מֵעַל תַחֲלֹץ נַעַלְךָ רַגְּלֶ֑ךָ in preceding clause), 20:3 ; יָחֵף הֹלֵךְ 2Sam 15:30 ; יָחֵף נָהַג Isa 20:3 ; apparently = substantive, מִיָּחֵף רַגְלֵךְ מִנְעִי Jer 2:25 withhold thy foot from bareness (Syriac discalceatio ). יַחְצְאֵלִי יַחֲצִיאֵל, יַחְצְאֵל, see below חצה .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to take off the shoes ;

occurrences.englishText: David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered, and went barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
at that time Yahweh spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, “Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.” He did so, walking naked and barefoot.
Yahweh said, “As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
